record.original_question: Does every 2-connected graph admit an embedding in some orientable surface such that every face boundary is a simple cycle?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.3 In some embedding of a 2-connected graph in an orientable surface, each face is bounded by a simple cycle.

artifact.self_contained_problem: A cellular embedding of a graph $G$ in a closed surface $S$ is a continuous injection of $G$ (viewed as a 1-complex) into $S$ such that every connected component of $S \setminus G$ (a face) is homeomorphic to an open disk. The boundary of a face is called a simple cycle if it is a cycle of $G$ with no repeated vertices or edges. Prove or disprove: every 2-connected graph $G$ admits a cellular embedding in some orientable closed surface in which every face is bounded by a simple cycle of $G$.
artifact.status_search_result: This is the Orientable Strong Embedding Conjecture. It implies both the Cycle Double Cover Conjecture and the (non-orientable) Strong Embedding Conjecture, and remains unresolved in general; partial results exist for special classes such as projective-planar graphs and cubic planar graphs.

status_evidence.title: Orientable Strong Embedding Conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: every 2-connected graph admits a cellular embedding in an orientable surface with all faces bounded by simple cycles
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is stated as an open problem and implies the Cycle Double Cover Conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Strong Embedding Conjecture (West)
status_evidence.snippet: Strong Embedding Conjecture: every 2-connected graph has an embedding in some surface in which every face is a simple cycle.

status_evidence.title: Orientable embeddings and orientable cycle double covers of projective-planar graphs
status_evidence.claim: Special cases verified but general conjecture remains open.
